title: Internet, Email and Cyber Terms: Protocols, Malware and the IT Act: Quiz

questions.question: Which protocol is used for SENDING email between servers?
questions.rationale: SMTP sends mail. POP3 and IMAP are used to receive or read it.

questions.question: Phishing carried out through SMS messages is called:
questions.rationale: Smishing uses SMS. Vishing uses voice calls and pharming redirects users to fake sites.

questions.question: In an email, a recipient placed in the Bcc field:
options: Is visible to all other recipients
questions.rationale: Bcc stands for blind carbon copy; the address is not shown to the others. Cc recipients are visible.

questions.question: Which malware disguises itself as useful software and does not replicate on its own?
questions.rationale: A Trojan relies on tricking the user into running it. A worm spreads by itself over a network.

questions.question: Which section of the IT Act, 2000 deals with punishment for cyber terrorism?
questions.rationale: 66F covers cyber terrorism, with punishment up to life imprisonment. 66C is identity theft, 66D cheating by personation and 66E privacy.

questions.question: What is the length of an IPv6 address?
questions.rationale: IPv6 uses 128 bits; IPv4 uses 32 bits.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a web browser?
questions.rationale: Google is a search engine, while Firefox, Edge and Opera are browsers. A browser views pages; a search engine finds them.

questions.question: The default port number of HTTPS is:
questions.rationale: HTTPS uses 443. Port 80 is HTTP, 21 is FTP and 25 is SMTP.

questions.question: Who sent the first ARPANET network email in 1971 and introduced the @ sign in addresses?
questions.rationale: Ray Tomlinson did so. Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web.

questions.question: In the URL https://www.example.gov.in/news/index.html, what is /news/index.html?
questions.rationale: It is the path to the page on the server. https is the protocol and example.gov.in is the domain.

questions.question: Ransomware is malware that:
options: Encrypts or locks data and demands payment
questions.rationale: Ransomware holds data hostage for payment. Adware shows adverts and a keylogger records keystrokes.

questions.question: Which of these correctly matches term and meaning?
options: DNS - converts domain names to IP addresses
questions.rationale: The Domain Name System resolves names to IP addresses. SSH, not FTP, is secure remote login.

questions.question: The IT Act, 2000 came into force on:
questions.rationale: It came into force on 17 October 2000. It was amended by the IT (Amendment) Act, 2008.

questions.question: A network of infected computers controlled remotely by an attacker is a:
questions.rationale: Botnets are commonly used for DDoS attacks and spam. A firewall is a defensive filter.

questions.question: Which statement about firewall is correct?
options: It is a type of virus
It filters incoming and outgoing network traffic
questions.rationale: A firewall monitors and filters traffic by rules. It is not a replacement for antivirus software.
